gap: No result ChatGPT got says which battery inverter can start which size of pump motor. The only horsepower figure any of our candidates' makers publish is Sun Gold Power's store listing: 'loaded motor capacity 6HP' for its 8 kW and 10 kW split-phase units and '4HP' for its 5000 W unit. The same store gives no HP figure for the SPH6548P or the 6000 W low-frequency unit, and AIMS and Signature Solar (EG4 6000XP) give none for theirs.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Franklin SubDrive/MonoDrive FAQ and the SubDrive Connect product page, plus the uncited SubDrive Connect manual (generator table on ManualsLib p.12) and the SubDrive Utility manual. All are Franklin variable-frequency-drive (VFD) documents. They cover drive input voltage (190–260 VAC), generator sizing (1.5× drive input watts; SubDrive20 Connect needs 5,700 W) and a warning that the SubDrive Utility is 'not compatible with inverter-controlled generators'. None of them pairs a battery inverter or inverter-charger with a pump horsepower, and none names a battery inverter. Rivals already cover the Franklin generator and input-voltage limits, so the new part is only the inverter-maker motor-HP data and the fact that most makers leave it out.
decides: It partly changes the picks. Of the products on our page, none has a maker-stated horsepower rating for motor loads. The page should not claim any of them starts a given HP. It can say Sun Gold rates its larger SPH units (8 kW/10 kW) at 6 HP of loaded motor and the 5000 W unit at 4 HP, so a shopper with a 1.5–2 HP 240 V pump who wants a maker number should look at the 8 kW SPH ($1,305, seen 2026-11-17) rather than the SPH6548P. A second point comes from combining sources: Franklin's FAQ says a SubDrive needs 190–260 VAC from L1 to L2, and Victron's MultiPlus-II 120V models are single 120 V units. So a single 120 V MultiPlus-II cannot feed a SubDrive or a 240 V pump without a second unit or an autotransformer.
